findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket are not encrypted at rest by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data if underlying storage or backups are compromised.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket storing ledger export data, meaning sensitive financial data is stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, leaving operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive operational/credential details) unencrypted at rest.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned S3 ACL name; this is likely a typo/misconfiguration and if it fails to apply or resolves unexpectedly it could leave the audit trail bucket without the intended restrictive access control, which is critical given it stores audit logs.

The object is uploaded to reports_archive, a bucket lacking server-side encryption configuration, and no per-object server_side_encryption is specified, so this vendor roster file is stored without encryption at rest.
